newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam set for record foreign investment in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam set for record foreign investment in 1996.

text.p: Vietnam is set to approve plans to build mini-cities on the outskirts of Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City, raising the value of foreign invested projects approved in 1996 to a record $9.7 billion, the Lao Dong newspaper said on Monday.
A Ministry of Planning and Investment official said licences for the two urban development projects, whose combined cost has been estimated at $3.1 billion, may be issued as early as Monday.

Earlier this year, the government played down figures showing an apparent slump in foreign investment after several years of rapid growth, saying there would be a rush of project approvals at the end of the year.
The value of projects with foreign investment approved last year was about $7.2 billion.

The $997.5 million project on the outskirts of Ho Chi Minh city, at An Phu-Thu Duc, is a joint venture between the state-owned Urban Development Service Company and Hong Kong's City Horse Trading Limited.
